method: Labelled by eye. Frames decoded read-only with OpenCV (the bundled FFmpeg build has no PNG encoder, tile or drawtext); timestamps are packet PTS from ffprobe minus the first frame's PTS. Kill-feed crop sampled every 0.5 s into 3x6 contact sheets (1.4x upscale, timestamp drawn on each tile) and every sheet was viewed; each own row was then pinned with a per-frame (1/30 s) strip of a tighter crop (x=640,y=55,w=320,h=60, 1.5x). t = first frame on which the row is visible, which is the solid-colour slide-in bar that precedes the full row by ~2 frames. Own rows = rows with the yellow outline/chevron on the player's side. Detector output was not consulted and no detector was run. Game mode looks like a 1v1 deathmatch-style mode ('FINAL STAGE' header): every row in the clip is between the player 'Me' and the opponent '<player>', and every one is an own row. Each row stays ~5 s and only one row is ever on screen. Both portraits look like Chamber; the death banners read 'KILLED BY CHAMBER'.

events.note: Row (shotgun icon) is already on screen at the first frame and gone by 0.6 s, so it is the tail of a row that appeared ~4.5 s before the clip starts; the kill itself is not in the clip. Kept so a detector that reports it at 0 is not penalised; drop it if pre-roll rows should not count.
